title: ECDSA serialization via g_ecdsa_fd_lock is a documented scalability bottleneck with no migration path
description:
DO_SIGN and DO_VERIFY can be called on ANY open crypto2dev fd — not just g_crypto2dev_fd. The kernel ioctl_do_sign() uses fget(op.key_fd) to reach the key fd and locks only key_state->lock (the KEY fd's own mutex). The calling fd is irrelevant. This is documented in the kernel source: 'These handlers hold only the KEY fd's mutex. They do NOT lock the calling fd's state because they operate entirely on the key fd's data.' (crypto2dev_fd.c:1193-1195).

The global g_ecdsa_fd_lock + g_crypto2dev_fd design in the port is therefore unnecessary. There is no kernel-side constraint requiring a single global fd for ECDSA — the constraint was invented by the port and defends nothing.

PLAN:
1. In crypto2dev_ecdsa(): replace the g_crypto2dev_fd + g_ecdsa_fd_lock pattern with crypto2dev_pool_acquire / ioctl DO_SIGN or DO_VERIFY on the pool fd / crypto2dev_pool_release. Same pattern as cipher and hash.
2. Remove g_ecdsa_fd_lock, g_ecdsa_fd_lock_inited globals.
3. Remove g_crypto2dev_fd global (only used for ECDSA after this change).
4. Remove ECDSA mutex init from wc_crypto2dev_init() and mutex cleanup from wc_crypto2dev_cleanup().
5. Remove the open() of g_crypto2dev_fd in wc_crypto2dev_init().
6. Update the comment block above g_ecdsa_fd_lock (now deleted) to remove the false claim that DO_SIGN only works on g_crypto2dev_fd.

Result: ECDSA sign/verify becomes as parallel as cipher/hash. Pool contention is shared but there is no new global serialization point. Concurrent DO_SIGN on different key fds runs with no shared lock. Concurrent DO_SIGN on the same key fd is serialized by that key fd's mutex — correct behavior.
